skill.name: project-scaffolding
skill.description: Creates new software projects through a guided scaffolding workflow. Supports web, mobile, backend, extension, serverless, monorepo, and library starters with common tooling templates.
skill.summary: Guided scaffolding for new web, mobile, backend, and tooling projects.
skill.author: hmohamed01

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from markdown examples, scaffold templates, placeholder environment documentation, and generated project code. Confirmed issues are limited to explicit native CLI command guidance and a real unvalidated output path in the Python scaffolder. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or hidden network behavior was found.

remediation.suggestion: Resolve the requested project path, reject absolute paths and parent traversal, and verify it remains under the intended base directory before creating files.
Require explicit user confirmation before running native CLI generators and prefer pinned versions or the local Python scaffolder when possible.

remediation.issue: Development secret defaults in generated templates
remediation.suggestion: Generate placeholders that fail production startup unless the user provides real secrets through a local environment file or secret manager.

content.value_statement: New projects often require many setup choices before useful work can begin. This skill guides those choices and creates starter files for common software stacks.
actual_capabilities: Guides project type, language, framework, database, and tooling choices.
Generates starter structures for static sites, frontend apps, backends, extensions, and monorepos.
Creates common files such as README, package metadata, gitignore, and environment examples.
Adds optional linting, testing, Docker, GitHub Actions, and Tailwind configuration templates.
Provides reference material for framework options and project organization patterns.
limitations: It does not validate the business logic of generated applications.
Some recommended native CLI generators can download dependencies when run.
Generated projects still require dependency installation and local verification.
Existing directory conflicts stop generation instead of merging changes.

use_cases.title: Start a frontend application
use_cases.description: Create a React, Next.js, Vue, Svelte, Astro, or Angular starter with selected styling and testing options.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap a backend service
use_cases.description: Set up an API project with framework, database, ORM, environment, Docker, and testing templates.

use_cases.title: Standardize team starters
use_cases.description: Generate repeatable project layouts with shared linting, formatting, CI, and documentation conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a static site
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a simple static website named portfolio-site with responsive CSS and a README.

prompt_templates.title: Create a React app
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a React TypeScript project named dashboard-app with Tailwind CSS, testing, linting, and formatting.

prompt_templates.title: Create a backend API
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a FastAPI project named orders-api with SQLAlchemy, PostgreSQL, Docker, pytest, and GitHub Actions.

prompt_templates.title: Create a monorepo
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Turborepo workspace named platform-suite with frontend, backend, shared packages, Docker, and CI templates.

output_examples.input: Create a React TypeScript dashboard project.
output: Creates a project folder with source, public, test, and configuration directories.
Adds package metadata for React, Vite, TypeScript, testing, and optional Tailwind CSS.
Adds README, gitignore, environment example, and starter application files.

output_examples.input: Create a FastAPI service with PostgreSQL.
output: Creates application, API, database, model, schema, and test folders.
Adds dependency files, environment example, Docker templates, and database configuration.
Includes starter route, settings, testing, and migration support files.
Creates extension source folders for popup, background, and content behavior.
Adds TypeScript and build tooling configuration for extension development.
Includes documentation for local development and packaging steps.

best_practices: Review generated configuration before installing dependencies or deploying the project.
Use a project name without path separators and keep output inside the workspace.
Replace placeholder secrets before running generated applications outside local development.
anti_patterns: Running unpinned package generator commands without user confirmation.
Putting real credentials into generated environment example files.
Scaffolding into parent directories or existing project folders.

faq.question: What project types does it support?
faq.answer: It covers static sites, frontend apps, backends, mobile apps, desktop apps, extensions, serverless functions, libraries, and monorepos.

faq.question: Does it run dependency installers automatically?
faq.answer: The Python scaffolder writes files. The skill also recommends native CLI generators, which should be run only with user confirmation.

faq.question: Can it add testing and linting?
faq.answer: Yes. It can include common testing, linting, formatting, and CI templates when those options are selected.

faq.question: Does it create production-ready secrets?
faq.answer: No. Generated secret values are placeholders and must be replaced before deployment.

faq.question: Can it update an existing project?
faq.answer: No. It is designed to create new project structures, not merge changes into existing codebases.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
